children: Crude oil slipped below $100 a barrel on Friday, likely reflecting a technical correction, but remained on track for a sharp weekly gain as escalating US-Iran tensions raised concerns over prolonged disruption to global energy supplies.

US officials have reportedly warned President Donald Trump that the conflict could extend through the remainder of his term, while Iranian leaders appear determined to continue fighting despite mounting economic costs.
Tehran has also claimed to have restored its missile capabilities and could intensify attacks on US and Gulf targets if Washington escalates.

Meanwhile, OPEC cut its forecast for global oil demand growth in 2026 to 380,000 barrels a day, marking its fifth consecutive downward revision, while the group’s output fell by 640,000 bpd in August. The IEA also lowered its outlook for Russian crude production, citing continued Ukrainian attacks on energy infrastructure, cutting its 2026 forecast by 125,000 bpd to 8.7 million bpd.

title: Crude Oil Heads for Sharp Weekly Rise
